Fixed #25010

Perhaps this is an acceptable solution...
pr_comments: Oh wait. I see @takahirox just suggested the same idea. :-)

I've also thought about adding this change when reading https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/25010 but I'm afraid this opens the door for adding even more global defaults. Devs could argue to add the same for other parameters and it's hard to argue against this if we merge this PR.

To me, I think the presented workaround in https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/25010#issuecomment-1327017463 sounds sufficient. An additional traverse should not be noticeable in terms of loading time.

Another solution may be...

* Test `.anisotropy > 1` and check visual quality and performance
* If visual quality benefit is big and performance penalty is small, change the hardcoded default `.anisotropy` to for example 4.

Regarding "opening tthe door for more globals", out of curiosity, I think it would still be on a case-by-case basis, right? And in some cases it may well make sense. Anisotropy as an example of a typical per-app default is kind of a good example for something that could be a global.

In Unity Anisotropy is also one of the few quality globals:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2693840/203962001-4210ecdd-1441-4489-9eb2-59a57ef46102.png)
(it has options "Disabled", "Per Texture", "Forced On")

issue_context.title: Ability to control `texture.anisotropy` from `GLTFLoader`
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We were often wondering why textures in three.js looked more blurry than in other engines. See for example the files in https://github.com/google/model-viewer/issues/1505. Turns out that while generally texture anisotropy can be set, GLTFLoader currently doesn't expose a way to control it, so glTF viewers generally look "kind of blurry" from steep angles.  
 
I'm happy to work on a PR for this but would like to align on possible solutions first.  

The renderer has `renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy` which contains the maximum allowed anisotropy, but I think being able to pass in an override for this into the loader would be nice instead of just setting the max (and there's currently no access to the renderer as far as I can see, minus spawning a new one).  

Currently I'm just adding `texture.anisotropy = 4;` in GLTFLoader.loadTextureImage so that it applies to textures loaded via extensions as well.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Some way to override texture anisotropy as used by GLTFLoader.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Adding some texture loading extension. Complexity would be that this would still need to work with all other texture loading extensions, so not entirely sure how that would work.  

- Iterating over all materials and all textures in the glTF file and setting anisotropy there. Harder than it should be in my opinion but maybe I'm missing a convenient way to do that.

If there's a good way to set this without changing GLTFLoader I'm all ears :)
comments:
Thanks for the comments! 
Sounds like the global may be the most useful solution here. Typically most textures do indeed have the same aniso value in an app.

Agree that it would be great if there's a regular way to get all textures that were loaded independent of extension; would you consider it a bug that `associations` / `getDependency` contain the wrong texture for `texture_transform` cases?

Iterating over material keys sounds doable but rather slow, plus there may be another fancy case: we have an extension that sets up custom shaders during loading, so theoretically one needs to traverse uniforms as well to really find all textures that way.

> would you consider it a bug that associations / getDependency contain the wrong texture for texture_transform cases?

For `getDependency` no (it's intended to return source textures in the file, not all variants cloned while parsing), but for `associations` yes.

I'm happy with the default idea suggested by @takahirox and @WestLangley  as well. (https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/25015)

review_comments: Hm, why the case differs between `Object3D.DefaultUp`/`Object3D.DefaultMatrixAutoUpdate` and `Texture.DEFAULT_IMAGE`/`Texture.DEFAULT_MAPPING`/`Texture.DEFAULT_ANISOTROPY`?

For the time being, it's sufficient when we adhere to naming conventions per file. At a later point, we can unify the syntax.
